correctness.rationale: An independent uniqueness-preserving recursion generated every monotone Boolean function through five variables; imposing \(v(\varnothing)=0\) and \(v(N)=1\) reproduced exactly 1, 4, 18, 166 and 7579 labeled simple games. Exact rational Banzhaf, Shapley--Shubik and Johnston computations show no Johnston weak-order divergence from either comparator for any game through four players and exactly 1870 divergent labeled games at five. Independent canonicalization of minimal-winning-coalition antichains under all 120 player permutations gives 208 five-player classes and 34 divergent classes. The minimum number of minimal winning coalitions among divergent games is three; all 30 such labeled games form one orbit. For the stated representative, the independently reconstructed normalized vectors are \((3,5,5,5,5)/23\), \((2/15,13/60,13/60,13/60,13/60)\), and \((1/8,11/48,11/48,5/24,5/24)\). Because the theorem is explicitly finite through five players, exhaustive enumeration is a complete proof rather than evidence for an infinite extrapolation.
